card.name: Words leading into route of administration
card.fires_on: Linking or verb words just before a route of administration such as subcutaneous, intravenous or oral, e.g. 'or', 'as', 'given', 'administered'. Also fires partway through the word subcutaneously.

modes.label: Linking word before a route
modes.description: Words like 'or' or 'as' that come right before a route term such as subcutaneously or oral.
modes.example: Naloxone hydrochloride injection may be administered intravenously, intramuscularly,<< or>> subcutaneously.

modes.label: Dose followed by giving verb
modes.description: A verb such as 'given' or 'administered' after a dose amount, before the route.
modes.example: The recommended dosage of depo-subQ provera 104 is 104 mg<< given>> subcutaneously every 12 to

modes.label: Inside subcutaneous
modes.description: The middle of the word subcutaneously, split into pieces.
modes.example: MITOXANTRONE SHOULD NOT BE ADMINISTERED SUBC<<UT>>ANEOUSLY.

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward a route word like subcutaneous, and away from pieces like 'se'.
card.plain: It lights up on small words right before the text names how a drug is given, especially under the skin.
